sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: This case examines the Confrontation Clause. It limits the use of out-of-court statements. The clause requires witnesses to face the accused. An exception exists for witness unavailability. The exception is called forfeiture by wrongdoing. The core question is the scope of this exception. Specifically, it asks if intent to silence is required.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the limits of the Confrontation Clause. It determines when out-of-court statements are admissible. It affects criminal trials involving unavailable witnesses. It clarifies the forfeiture by wrongdoing exception. It impacts the rights of the accused. It shapes the rules for admitting hearsay evidence.
